articles.title: Nations League: Greece stun Klopp’s Germany, Netherlands sink Serbia but Gakpo hurt
articles.summary: Jürgen Klopp ‘unbothered’ despite 1-0 home defeat. Gakpo goes off in 2-1 win, Portugal edge past Norway. Greece stunned hosts Germany 1-0 in Augsburg to go top of their Nations League group and spoil Jürgen Klopp’s debut in the home dugout.
body: Dimitris Kourbelis scored the only goal in the 74th minute, earning Greece their first-ever victory in 11 matches against Germany. Ivan Jovanovic’s side now lead ⁠Group A2 with six points ⁠from two matches; Klopp’s side are third with one point from two games after a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands on Thursday.

The hosts were in control for most of the game and had close to 80% possession in the first half alone. Germany were ultimately punished ⁠for sloppy defending, especially in the second half, which gave the visitors space to attack.

Felix Nmecha fired wide in the 54th minute, moments after the Greece keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis ‌had palmed a Joshua Kimmich free kick over the bar. The Greeks then almost scored in the 66th after Kimmich lost possession in his own half, but substitute Fotis Ioannidis fired just wide of the post.

They did better eight minutes later, with Kourbelis’ deflected low drive earning their second victory in a row after their last-gasp 2-1 win over Serbia on Thursday. Greece will now host the Dutch on Thursday, while Germany host Serbia.
points: Gakpo goes off in 2-1 win, Portugal edge past Norway.
Greece stunned hosts Germany 1-0 in Augsburg to go top of their Nations League group and spoil Jürgen Klopp’s debut in the home dugout.
Dimitris Kourbelis scored the only goal in the 74th minute, earning Greece their first-ever victory in 11 matches against Germany.
Ivan Jovanovic’s side now lead ⁠Group A2 with six points ⁠from two matches; Klopp’s side are third with one point from two games after a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands on Thursday.

articles.title: McTominay’s role a poser for Pocognoli as Scotland offer positives in Slovenia
articles.summary: New coach still learning about his squad as they prepare to face Switzerland with the Napoli midfielder expected to return in November. An elongated international window does not prevent Sébastien Pocognoli from glancing towards the next one.
body: The scoreless draw in Slovenia on Saturday raised the question of where McTominay will fit in when he returns. “He can play in many positions,” Pocognoli said. “He is a top player so he can read the game. We will see.”

Indeed we will. The answer is not immediately obvious. Pocognoli deployed Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson as central midfielders in Ljubljana with John McGinn placed ahead of them to support a two-man strike force. Gilmour was heavily influential during Scotland’s impressive second half. Ferguson’s combative and defensive skills are valuable. McGinn, like McTominay, is a mainstay of the team. It is therefore legitimate to ask how Pocognoli handles McTominay, who is expected to return to the Scotland scene in November.

“For now we just need to put the structure in place,” Pocognoli said. “I hope Scott watched the game and thought ‘OK, I see myself in that shape in the second half’, and that with good discipline he can enjoy it. I hope he can look and think: ‘Yeah, I want to play.’
“Andy Robertson was really positive after the game and said that he really enjoyed it. It is really good to hear that from top players.”
points: New coach still learning about his squad as they prepare to face Switzerland with the Napoli midfielder expected to return in November.
An elongated international window does not prevent Sébastien Pocognoli from glancing towards the next one.

articles.title: No handshakes between Republic of Ireland and Israel
articles.summary: The Republic of Ireland and Israel players do not shake hands with each other before or after Sunday's controversial Uefa Nations League game in Hungary.
body: Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson said his players "raised awareness worldwide" after they chose not to engage in pre-match formalities with Israel.
The Republic of Ireland and Israel players did not shake hands before Sunday's Uefa Nations League game in Hungary and the Irish players bowed their heads when Israel's anthem was played.
There was also no exchange of pennants between Republic of Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel skipper Manor Solomon, who did not shake hands.
The fixtures have been embroiled in controversy since February when the two teams were drawn to play each other in Group B3.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland put controversy aside to earn impressive win over Israel
articles.summary: Football and politics are inseparable in the modern world, no matter how many people wish they were not. But whether the beautiful game can ease the ills of our age is another matter.
body: In the end the result was indeed a walkover, just not because of a ­boycott. On Saturday night the ­question had been whether Heimir Hallgrimsson’s side would take to the field in Hungary at all. If they did, would their heads be in the game? It turned out that a week of internal angst had been enough to produce collective resolve among the Irish squad, or at least those selected to play. Strong and assertive from the off, their forwards each scored in the first half to settle the ­contest, with plenty of symbolic action to assure those back home of their feelings.

“It’s probably been the ­toughest days of my coaching career,” ­Hallgrimsson said after the match. “But it’s not about me. It’s about the players and they’ve shown today how much ­playing for Ireland means to them. They ­represented themselves on the pitch with dignity but also with the power of proud Irishmen. They’ve shown today how much playing for Ireland means to them and hopefully they will have the support of the Irish people.”

articles.title: USA’s McNulty transcends chaos of Montreal road race to claim ‘miracle’ world title
articles.summary: Arizona rider first US champion since Lance Armstrong. Pre-race favourite Evenpoel fails to add second gold. Brandon McNulty, a UAE Emirates teammate of Tadej Pogacar, succeeded the Slovene as world champion with an unexpected solo win in the men’s UCI road race in Montreal.
body: In the biggest triumph of his career, the 28-year-old American took his country’s first win in the UCI’s blue riband event since Lance Armstrong’s lone victory in Oslo in 1993.

“I’m really at a loss,” McNulty said. “Until the last hundred metres, I didn’t believe it, I was so tired. I was just dying, but I kept pushing. We have said for weeks now that we had a super strong team. We talked about it, but I knew it would take a miracle. I guess miracles happen.”

McNulty’s 50-second lead at the start of the closing lap of the hilly Montreal circuit was enough to hold on to the finish line, despite a last‑ditch attempt by Tom Pidcock to chase down the American that, at one point, reduced his advantage to only a handful of seconds.

Pidcock was one of the animators of the final hour of racing, which followed the same volatile and unpredictable pattern as the women’s road race on Saturday, which was won by Demi Vollering of the Netherlands. A gruelling race, ridden without the benefit of race radios, was at times chaotic, particularly within the Belgium team’s confused tactics, with the Olympic road race champion, Remco Evenepoel, left once again to ponder what might have been.

articles.summary: Northern Ireland netball vice-captain Caroline O'Hanlon says "not many outside of our camp expected us to qualify" after the booked their spot in the 2027 World Cup in Australia.
body: Northern Ireland netball vice-captain Caroline O'Hanlon said "not many outside of our camp expected us to qualify" after the side booked their spot for the 2027 World Cup in Australia.
Sheonah Forbes' side secured their place in Sydney after beating Wales and the Republic of Ireland during their impressive qualifying campaign in East Kilbride.
It will be the first World Cup for Northern Ireland since 2019, after they missed out on the 2023 edition in Cape Town.
"There wouldn't have been many outside of our camp who expected us to qualify," O'Hanlon told BBC Sport NI.

articles.title: USA captain credits Trump for inspiring comeback victory at Presidents Cup
articles.summary: U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker credited U.S. President Donald Trump for inspiring the Americans to a thrilling Presidents Cup comeback victory over the International Team.
body: An 11th straight victory for the USA came after big surges on the back nine by two-time major champion Collin Morikawa and 21-year-old rookie Jackson Koivun.
And despite being outplayed for three days in the team golf format, the USA dominated the singles to claw back a three-point deficit and win 17-13.
Captain Snedeker then praised Trump for his impact, having seen the President welcome his players on the first tee at Medinah with the home fans creating a raucous atmosphere.
“All these guys fought for each other, fought for this country, fought for this team,” Snedeker said. “And one last shout to Donald Trump, President Trump.

articles.summary: Doubt crept in at Chelsea last season when they lost their Women's Super League crown - but early signs in this campaign suggest they have regained their spark for another challenge.
body: A crucial 1-0 victory over rivals Arsenal on Sunday meant they extended their WSL unbeaten run to 12 games and sit just two points off leaders Manchester City.
They showed a different side - one that was willing to dig deep, control the game without the ball and defend with composure while Arsenal put pressure on.
It may have been the missing ingredient as Chelsea look revitalised and refreshed.
Could they win the WSL title this year? It would be foolish to say they can't.

articles.title: Mariners manager Dan Wilson tells team he'll be fired | Report
articles.summary: Dan Wilson, who managed the Seattle Mariners to the brink of their first World Series appearance yet oversaw a significant regression the following season, told his team he will be fired as manager before the team's Sunday, Sept. 27 season finale, the Seattle Times reported.
body: The Mariners' 2026 season began with great expectations, but devolved into disappointment and ultimately concluded with the end of Wilson's reign.

Wilson, 57, took over for the fired Scott Servais for the final 34 games of the 2024 season and assumed the job on a permanent basis, leading the Mariners to 90 wins and the AL West championship in 2025. The Mariners held a 3-2 lead over the Toronto Blue Jays in the AL Championship Series, but lost Game 6 and blew a 3-1 seventh-inning lead in Game 7 as a handful of Wilson's managerial moves backfired, culminating in George Springer 's go-ahead three-run homer.

Still, the club had designs on going at least a step further this season, with a loaded pitching staff, a re-signed Josh Naylor and a trade for Brendan Donovan that galvanized the infield. None of it worked out: Cal Raleigh backslid from a 60-homer season to batting.182 with just 23 homers, Donovan was frequently injured and several members of the pitching staff regressed.

articles.title: KP promises to challenge McCullum as England push to be 'world's best'
articles.summary: Kevin Pietersen has promised to challenge England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum in his new role as a specialist mentor to the team, saying it's precisely why he was brought in.
body: Since retiring as a player in 2018, Pietersen has, at times, been an outspoken critic of the England setup, including when accusing the white-ball team of inadequate preparation on a tour of India last January after McCullum had just taken over.

Pietersen's work with England began with a 3-0 T20 series whitewash of Sri Lanka, before the hosts then also clinched a 2-1 ODI series success over the same side on Sunday. His role with the team will continue through to the 2027 50-over World Cup in just over a year's time.

"Brendon, when he first called me, I thought I was in trouble because I'd said something, but he said this exact point: 'I'd like you to come in and challenge me,'" Pietersen told Sky Sports Cricket ahead of England's series-clinching 223-run win over Sri Lanka at The Oval.
"He's since said to me: 'I absolutely love the fact that you are inside the rooms and you are picking on things that can make the players better.'

articles.title: 4 Takeaways From The New York Giants’ Ugly 12-7 Victory Over The Tennessee Titans
articles.summary: It was as ugly a game as you will see in the NFL this season. But when the clock expired, the scoreboard read New York Giants 12, Tennessee Titans 7. It was a pretty sight for Giants fans.
body: After getting soundly defeated by the Los Angeles Rams 28-6 on Monday night and losing Jaxson Dart for the season with a knee injury, the last thing the team needed was another loss. With sloppy field conditions affecting both teams, New York made the plays when it mattered most and came away with the victory.
However, the victory could prove to be a costly one as Brian Burns left the game in the 4 th quarter with a knee injury. Here’s our take on the biggest takeaways from Big Blue’s victory.
With Dart out, the most effective way New York will be able to move the ball this season is with their running game. On Sunday, they ran the ball 33 times for 137 yards.

With Devin Singletary as a surprise scratch, New York’s running game was spearheaded by Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris. Skattebo ran the ball 20 times for 60 yards, and Harris rushed the ball nine times for 52 yards.

articles.title: Kohli passes 15,000 ODI runs as hundred helps India beat West Indies
articles.summary: Virat Kohli celebrated his return to the international arena by hitting his 55th ODI hundred as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in the series opener on Sunday.
body: India's star batter - who now only plays this format in international cricket - smashed an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls, including 10 fours and nine sixes, as India successfully chased down 296 in just 41.4 overs.
In doing so, the 37-year-old also became only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar (18,426) to pass 15,000 runs in ODIs.

"My focus has never been on milestones. Just looking back at the start of my journey, it makes me feel very grateful," Kohli said. "I enjoy each and every minute that I am out there playing for India, and I am able to do the job for my team. As a cricketer, this is all I could dream of."
Skipper Shubman Gill also notched a century, scoring 110 off 108 deliveries as India registered an easy win - clinched with a Kohli six - to go 1-0 up in the three-match series.

articles.title: Australia suffer ODI series defeat to South Africa
articles.summary: Australia fell to an ODI series defeat to South Africa with a game to spare as they were beaten by 32 runs in the second ODI match of three in Johannesburg on Sunday.
body: David Miller (142 off 93 balls) and Temba Bavuma (103 off 116) each smashed centuries for South Africa as they set the visitors a massive 366-run target after being inserted at the toss.
Australia looked well placed early on in their reply, with openers Mitch Marsh (84 off 53) and ​Travis Head (85 off 76) setting the tone by blazing the bowling to all parts.

But ultimately the tourists' middle-order batting issues and struggles against spin were again laid bare. From 191-2 in the 25th over, they added only 62 for the loss of four wickets in the next 15 and a bit overs to stumble to 253-6.

That left Australia needing another 113 runs to win from the final 10 overs and, despite a late counter-punch from Xavier Bartlett (50 off 28), they'd eventually be bowled out for 333 in the final over.

videos.title: The advantages of being 5-foot-3
videos.summary: At 5-foot-3, how did Muggsy Bogues turn his height into an advantage — and build a 14-year NBA career?
body: Muggsy joins Ben Taylor of Thinking Basketball in our latest episode of "Anatomy of the Game" to reveal how he used timing, angles and his low center of gravity to thrive against much bigger opponents.

Together, they revisit his 18-point, 17-assist, 4-steal performance against the powerful duo of Penny Hardaway, Shaquille O’Neal and the eventual Eastern Conference champion Orlando Magic during the 1994–95 season but also revisit film of memorable matchups against Michael Jordan, Reggie Miller and more.

Muggsy explains how he picked elite ballhandlers’ pockets, held his ground against taller players in the post, deceived defenders with his eyes and attacked driving angles others simply couldn't access. Go inside the decisions and techniques that helped him not only make the NBA, but last in the league as a high-impact floor general and starter in his prime.
